correctness.rationale: For a linear word, two deleted positions yield the same descendant exactly when they lie in the same maximal constant run. Deleting a double run always stays legal; deleting an interior singleton violates the receiver cap precisely if equal flanking run symbols merge to length at least three. The four-state weights enumerate the middle run upon appending its right neighbor, with q-2 non-repeating and one repeating symbol. For min degree, with k double runs, b surviving singleton deletions, t invalid singletons, and e double endpoint runs: d=k+b, n=2k+b+t, t<=2k-e, b>=2-e imply n<=4d-2. Constructive run words meet equality at every n, and at n=4h-2 equality forces double endpoints and exactly two invalid singleton runs per adjacent pair of doubles; symbol choices count q(q-1)^(h-1). Max degree n iff all runs singleton. The packaged exhaustive checker reproduces local, transfer and direct methods for 115544 admissible words; finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: A receiver required to retain the same physical run-length constraint changes the one-deletion read graph and the number of distinct admissible outputs in ways not captured by the ordinary deletion-run formula. The exact all-length local-degree spectrum, tight minimum degree, and rigidity/count of sharp minimizers at a complete congruence family provide a motivated structural statistic for constrained channel robustness and deletion-read ambiguity, rather than an arbitrary short numerical slice or a routine restatement of a known unfiltered sphere.
